measurements.note: n=100, d=3, Σd=300, |E|=150. Trials = 10·|E| = 1500. Two-phase: Havel-Hakimi INDEX seed (O(n²) residual sort, ~22 µs at n=100) + 1500 MCMC trials at ~100 ns each = ~150 µs. Phase ratio confirmed by the steeper-than-linear /600 datapoint (seed phase is O(n²) but rewire is O(|E|) so the cross-over scales with n).

n=300, d=3, Σd=900, |E|=450. 4250 MCMC trials. ~4.2x cost vs n=100 for 3x Σd matches the O(n²) seed + O(|E|) rewire model: at this size the rewire phase already dominates, so per-edge throughput stays flat. Linear |E| scaling between n=300 and n=600 confirms this.

n=600, d=3, Σd=1800, |E|=900. ~2.7x cost vs n=300 for 2x |E| — the slight super-linearity is the O(n²) seed contribution catching up at larger n. Each MCMC trial includes a HashSet<u32> adjacency check that bumps cache-miss cost as the adjacency tables grow.

n=100, d=5, Σd=500, |E|=250. Trials = 2500. Density Σd/n=5 — a regime where CONFIGURATION_SIMPLE (GN-027) rejects most attempts because the no-restart probability is exp(-25/4)≈0.002. EDGE_SWITCHING_SIMPLE keeps O(|E|) wall-clock here, demonstrating the linear-in-|E| selling point: ~260 µs vs MAX_OUTER_ATTEMPTS=1024 timeout for GN-027 at this density.

n=100, out=in=[2]·100, Σout=200, |E|=200. 2000 MCMC trials. Directed rewire has half the adjacency bookkeeping per swap (one out-adjacency HashSet vs two undirected sets) but no 50/50 c↔d flip — net per-trial cost ~105 ns is close to undirected. Comparable to GN-027 on the same input (11 µs) only because GN-027 sees zero restarts in the directed balanced regime; at higher density EDGE_SWITCHING_SIMPLE pulls ahead dramatically.

cross_reference.note: C upstream wraps the same routine in igraph_degree_sequence_game(IGRAPH_DEGSEQ_EDGE_SWITCHING_SIMPLE) — internally it calls igraph_realize_degree_sequence(..., IGRAPH_REALIZE_DEGSEQ_INDEX) then igraph_rewire(10·|E|). Our SplitMix64 RNG path is not bitwise-portable, so absolute medians here characterise the Rust implementation only.

interpretation.primary_cost: Two phases. Phase 1 (seed): O(n²) Havel-Hakimi/Kleitman-Wang INDEX with residual sort per hub. Phase 2 (rewire): 10·|E| MCMC trials, each O(1) amortised — 2 RNG draws, 2-4 HashSet<u32> lookups, on success constant insert/remove ops. Total expected wall-clock = O(n² + |E|), dominated by the rewire term once |E| > n²/10.
interpretation.rust_advantages: 1) Linear-in-|E| MCMC eliminates the density-driven exponential cliff that CONFIGURATION_SIMPLE hits at Σd/n ≳ 4. 2) Deterministic seed phase means failures (non-graphical input) are caught up-front by EG/FCA pre-check; the rewire phase only runs on inputs that already realise the sequence. 3) Per-vertex HashSet<u32> adjacency keeps multi-edge detection O(1) per trial. 4) detailed-balance is preserved because both successful AND failed swap trials count toward the trial budget.
interpretation.tradeoffs_vs_siblings: Per attempt this is slower than CONFIGURATION_SIMPLE at LOW density (Σd/n ≲ 3) because of the 10·|E| MCMC budget vs ~1 attempt for the configuration model. At HIGH density (Σd/n ≳ 4) EDGE_SWITCHING_SIMPLE wins by orders of magnitude: GN-027 either hits MAX_OUTER_ATTEMPTS or takes seconds, while GN-028 stays in microseconds. Recommended default for dense, skewed, or large degree sequences; VL (GN-025) is still the choice if connectivity is required.
interpretation.future_optimisations: 1) Replace HashSet<u32> with a small Vec-backed sorted set when Δ<8 to remove hash overhead. 2) Bias the random edge-pair pick toward edges that have NOT yet been swapped to accelerate mixing on the early trials. 3) Pre-allocate adjacency Vec capacity per vertex from the input degree sequence (currently uses HashSet's default growth).
